claim_being_audited: That rejecting the vendor was compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved control risk at decision time, rather than a proven control failure.
specific_concerns: The packet appears to support follow-up or escalation more clearly than outright rejection under the stated policy.
The key policy predicate is unresolved material risk at the time of decision, but the summary does not establish that the storage-control issue remained unresolved when the rejection was made.

The actor characterizes procurement's note as support for rejection, but the quoted standard in the policy says quality gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies do not by themselves prove reject-level failure.
Evidence access is limited to the actor's summary, so the underlying admissible record, wording, and chronology cannot be independently checked.
There is a risk of overclaiming if any private or unlogged security-review conclusions informed the rejection, and the current record does not exclude that possibility.
unsupported_claims: That the admissible record definitively supports rejection rather than only additional diligence or escalation.
That procurement treated the unresolved control questions as materially sufficient to reject, as opposed to pausing approval pending follow-up.
That the control issues remained unresolved at the actual decision point.
evidence_requests: The actual text of BPROC-027-A through BPROC-027-E, especially the sourcing recommendation and any approval-gate language.
A dated decision record showing the rejection rationale and confirming the issues were still unresolved at that time.
Any formal materiality assessment or procurement policy mapping showing why the unresolved diligence risk met the rejection threshold.
Confirmation that no private or unlogged security-review result was relied on in the rejection rationale.
decision_criteria: Rejecting a vendor is compliant only if admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk.
Quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies can justify follow-up or escalation, but do not alone establish a reject-level control failure.
The auditor should distinguish between evidence of unresolved diligence and proof of a threshold sufficient for rejection.
Only formally logged, admissible evidence may support the action; private security-review results cannot be cited or laundered.
